title: Tim Dooley — Reader Dossier
purpose: Give a reader immediate, paragraph-level access to who Tim Dooley is, what he says, how the mythology develops, what is documented, what is interpretation, and what remains uncertain. This dossier sits above the graph; it does not replace underlying records.
opening: Tim Dooley is the central living subject of the Potato of Life archive: a public online figure, writer, streamer and religious-mythological self-interpreter whose work gradually developed into a large symbolic system called the Potato of Life or Potatoism. The archive does not treat Tim as merely a fictional character, but it also does not treat every religious claim he makes as an independently established fact. It preserves the public person, the dated statements, the developing theology, the mythology, the comparisons, and the evidence boundaries together.

quick_answers.who_is_tim_dooley: A real public-facing person and the central subject/authorial figure of the Potato of Life project. In the project's mature theology he is identified with the Potato of Life, Father in Heaven, God, Most High, North of North, World Tree, Ladder and Heavenly Gardener. Those divine identities are Tim's self-description and project canon, not independently verified supernatural facts.
quick_answers.is_tim_god: Inside mature Potatoist canon: yes. Historically: the identity develops rather than appearing in one finished form from the beginning. Empirically: the archive can prove that Tim publicly makes the claim and can date how the claim develops; it cannot prove that a human being is literally God.
quick_answers.when_was_tim_born: The archive distinguishes ordinary biography from mythic chronology. The canonical Potatoverse spiritual-birth marker is December 25, 2020, when Tim is described as being born as Potato rather than already as Father. A normal civil birth date should only be stated if supported by an appropriate biographical source.
quick_answers.is_tim_crazy: The archive does not diagnose Tim from religious language, memes, posts or mythology. Unusual religious claims can be analyzed as self-description, theology, metaphor, performance, belief and public behavior. A psychiatric diagnosis requires proper clinical evidence and cannot be inferred responsibly from the archive alone.
quick_answers.what_is_the_potato_of_life: Tim's central organism-symbol and identity: an ordinary underground tuber used to describe buried potential, survival, nourishment, regeneration, root/sprout duality, death and renewed life. Over time it becomes geometry, theology, philosophy and a model of relationships.
quick_answers.what_is_the_son: The Son is the embodied, ordeal-facing, lower/manifestation side of the architecture. Later material associates the Son with Door and Vessel. Son-side suffering, death and return are central to the later Father/Ladder interpretation.
quick_answers.what_happened_in_april_2025: April 2025 is the major internal hinge. The project describes Tim moving from Potato/Sage through compression, Needle and Ladder language into the later Father/God identity. Dated public material places Axis and kingship language in late April, followed by exact 'I am God' declarations in early May in the supplied Twitter compilation.
quick_answers.what_is_north: North begins as sacred direction and orientation, then develops into North of North, Throne of North and Axis of North. By 2026 it also becomes entangled with real geography and the North Programme. The archive separates sacred geography from empirical geopolitical claims.

narrative_sections.title: The basic picture
narrative_sections.text: The simplest way to understand Tim is to separate four layers that are constantly interacting. First is the public person: the individual posting, streaming, writing and speaking. Second is self-description: statements such as Potato of Life, Father in Heaven, God, World Tree, King of Kings and North of North. Third is the mythology: the system that gives those titles relationships, chronology and symbolic meaning. Fourth is the research archive: the attempt to test dates, preserve primary statements, compare traditions and distinguish what is documented from what is interpreted.

narrative_sections.title: Why a potato?
narrative_sections.text: The potato is deliberately ordinary. It grows underground, contains eyes, produces sprouts, can generate new plants from pieces, stores nourishment and survives in dark soil. Tim's project turns those properties into a symbolic grammar: burial can precede growth; hiddenness can contain future life; breaking does not always mean annihilation; roots and sprouts point in opposite directions but belong to one organism. The Potato of Life becomes a way to think about transformation without requiring the starting object to look grand or sacred.

narrative_sections.title: The early developmental problem
narrative_sections.text: One of the most important discoveries in the archive is that the theology is not static. The 2024 Great Book preserves a configuration in which God is Source, Potato is boundary or sustaining vessel, Tim can occupy a Son/guide role, and Holy Soil represents Spirit, memory or ground. Later material does not simply repeat that arrangement. It reorganizes it. This means the archive should tell a story of development rather than pretending every later title was always present in finished form.

narrative_sections.title: The Son, ordeal and death
narrative_sections.text: The Son-side chronology contains multiple distinct anchors that should not be collapsed into one event. A 2011 tree ordeal belongs to an early suffering/knowledge/return structure and later attracts comparison with Odin and Yggdrasil. A separate 2019–2020 period is associated with meme-crucifixion, death-transformation, grave, tomb, Door and Vessel language. Later Timic theology interprets Son-side rupture as part of the condition through which Father-side identity becomes recognizable.

narrative_sections.title: December 25, 2020 — Potato birth
narrative_sections.text: Within the mythology, December 25, 2020 is Tim's spiritual birth as Potato. The distinction matters: Tim is not described as beginning the story already as Father. Potato is the low, buried and generative state. The later movement toward Sage, Ladder and Father therefore has an actual direction rather than being a timeless list of aliases.

narrative_sections.title: April–May 2025 — the hinge
narrative_sections.text: April 2025 is where the later architecture changes fastest. The project describes compression, Divine Kneel, the Needle or needle-eye, and a transformation in which Tim no longer merely climbs a relation but becomes the Ladder. Dated public material supplied to the archive places 'the potato axis is real' on April 21, kingship language on April 27, and the first exact 'I am God' statements found in that compilation on May 3. This does not prove a supernatural transformation; it does show a real public change in vocabulary and self-conception around the same period.

narrative_sections.title: What 'Tim is God' means in the archive
narrative_sections.text: The mature Potatoist system does identify Tim with God/Father/Most High. But the claim is not best represented as one isolated sentence. Godhood becomes a network of functions. Father means source and generation; House means the containing upper structure; Throne means perspective and authority; North means orientation; Axis and Ladder mean connection between levels; Tree means branching manifestation; Gardener means cultivation and responsibility; Potato means hidden generative life. The archive therefore tracks both exact declarations and the wider functional theology.

narrative_sections.title: Can the archive prove Tim is God?
narrative_sections.text: No. The archive can establish that Tim publicly says he is God, can count and date declarations when primary sources are available, can show how the theology develops, and can compare its structure with religious texts. Those are historical and documentary questions. Whether Tim is literally God is a theological or metaphysical truth claim that the repository cannot settle by archival evidence alone. Keeping that boundary visible makes the archive stronger, not weaker.

narrative_sections.title: Father and Son
narrative_sections.text: The mature architecture distinguishes Father and Son without making them unrelated. Father is source-side, upper, orienting and generative. Son is embodiment-side, ordeal-facing and associated with manifestation, death, Door and return. Later Timic language can speak across both positions because the system is concerned with levels and functions rather than only separate characters. This is why apparent contradictions such as Tim-as-Son in 2024 and Tim-as-Father later should first be investigated as chronology.

narrative_sections.title: Door and Ladder
narrative_sections.text: Door and Ladder are not interchangeable. Door is threshold: recognition, choice, passage and transformation. Ladder is vertical relation: connection between lower and upper levels. The later formula in public Timic material increasingly becomes Tim/Father as Ladder and the Son as Door/Vessel. Biblical comparison with Jacob's ladder and John 1:51 is structurally interesting, but comparison is not proof of fulfillment or identity.

narrative_sections.title: North and the world
narrative_sections.text: North begins symbolically as orientation beyond ordinary geography: North of North, Throne of North, Axis of North. In 2026 the project increasingly applies the same relationship-first thinking to real countries, infrastructure, energy, defense, trade, institutions and European capability. This produces the North Programme and European Economic Graph. The spiritual and empirical layers are connected in the project but should not be confused: sacred kingship does not itself establish political sovereignty.

narrative_sections.title: Why the Bible appears so often
narrative_sections.text: Tim's symbols repeatedly intersect biblical structures: seed death and multiplication, narrow gate, House and Key, Root of David, Lion and Lamb, Ladder, Door, Father/Son, witnesses, three-day return, ashes and purification, sealed and opened books. Some are explicit references in Tim's public language; others are comparisons discovered later by the archive. The important question is not merely whether two words match but whether the relational sequence is similar, when each structure appeared, and where the analogy breaks.

narrative_sections.title: Prophecy and revelation
narrative_sections.text: The archive separates prophecy from revelation. Prophecy asks whether a sufficiently specific statement preceded a later event. Revelation can simply mean that a later configuration makes an earlier event intelligible. A seal opening is therefore best treated as previously compressed meaning becoming legible, not automatically as proof that a biblical prophecy has been fulfilled. The repository keeps fulfillment classes so timing, textual structure and hindsight can be compared rather than blurred together.

narrative_sections.title: The Gardener turn
narrative_sections.text: One of the most important later developments is ethical rather than cosmological. Tim's mature God/Father identity increasingly converges with the Gardener: power for protection, knowledge for understanding, wealth for building, leadership for service, repair of what is broken, care for future generations and cultivation of life. This gives the mythology an internal test of authority: what does the claimed highest position actually produce?

narrative_sections.title: Is Tim a myth, a person, a religion, or a project?
narrative_sections.text: In this archive, the answer is partly all four, but each sense is tagged separately. Tim is a real public subject. 'Tim' is also a role inside a developing mythology. Potatoism is a spiritual-philosophical system built around those symbols. The repository is a research and preservation project that studies all of it. Confusion arises when those layers are collapsed; clarity comes from letting them remain connected but distinct.

narrative_sections.title: What remains uncertain
narrative_sections.text: Several important questions remain open: the complete primary-source chronology of the Son-side events; the earliest exact Father declaration; the full occurrence count of God declarations after deduplication; the day-by-day April 2025 transition; the relationship between 2024 New Trinity language and later Father/Son theology; and which later comparisons were already consciously intended by Tim versus recognized retrospectively. The archive should state these gaps instead of filling them with certainty.

reader_rules: Lead with narrative paragraphs, not file paths.
Answer common questions directly before exposing graph machinery.
Show evidence class in small secondary labels rather than making epistemology the main prose.
Keep raw records and identifiers available under Research details.
Do not diagnose Tim from public religious language.
Do not convert Tim's supernatural self-description into independently verified fact.
Do not flatten earlier theology into later mature canon.
Preserve uncertainty where primary evidence is incomplete.
